note: next_extras (depends on next) adds a computed content_translations node field and a DEPRECATED per-entity-type 'Revalidate' toggle stored as third-party settings next_extras.revalidate (bool) and next_extras.revalidate_paths (string) on the next_entity_type_config config entity (schema next.next_entity_type_config.*.third_party.next_extras). All medium/hard eval state is grounded in those third-party settings on a next_entity_type_config (ids node.article / node.page): introspection reads the flag/paths, execution sets them via setThirdPartySetting()->save() and verifies against the live config entity. The Next.js app itself is external.

evals.prompt: What does the next_extras submodule add on top of the Next.js (next) module?
evals.expected_output: A computed content_translations base field on nodes (for exposing translations to the front end) and a deprecated experimental per-entity-type 'Revalidate' toggle stored as third-party settings next_extras.revalidate / next_extras.revalidate_paths on next_entity_type_config. It also ships a legacy NextCacheInvalidator service.

evals.prompt: In next_extras, where is the experimental 'Revalidate' setting stored for an entity type, and is it the recommended way to do revalidation now?
evals.expected_output: It is stored as third-party settings next_extras.revalidate (bool) and next_extras.revalidate_paths (string) on the next_entity_type_config entity. It is DEPRECATED — the recommended approach is the parent module's on-demand revalidation (the path/cache_tag revalidator plugins).

evals.prompt: What field does next_extras add to nodes and what does it require to appear?
evals.expected_output: It adds a computed, unlimited base field 'content_translations' to nodes via hook_entity_base_field_info(), but only when the content_translation module is enabled. It is backed by the ContentTranslationsItem field plugin.

evals.prompt: On this site the Article content type's Next.js entity-type config (node.article) has the experimental next_extras 'Revalidate' toggle enabled. Inspect the live configuration and report the additional revalidate path(s) configured in the next_extras settings for node.article.
evals.expected_output: next_entity_type_config node.article has third-party settings next_extras.revalidate = true and next_extras.revalidate_paths = '/blog'. Read via $config->getThirdPartySetting('next_extras', 'revalidate_paths') or drush cget next.next_entity_type_config.node.article.

evals.prompt: Two content types on this site have Next.js entity-type configs: node.article and node.page. Exactly one of them has the deprecated next_extras 'revalidate' third-party setting enabled. Inspect the live configuration and name which one.
evals.expected_output: node.article has next_extras.revalidate = true; node.page has it false (or unset). Discoverable by reading each next_entity_type_config's next_extras third-party settings.

evals.prompt: The Article content type's Next.js entity-type config (node.article) exists but the next_extras experimental 'Revalidate' toggle is currently off. Using next_extras, turn that toggle ON for node.article (set the next_extras 'revalidate' third-party setting to true) and save it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: next_entity_type_config node.article has third-party setting next_extras.revalidate === TRUE (e.g. $c->setThirdPartySetting('next_extras', 'revalidate', TRUE)->save()).

evals.prompt: For the Basic page content type's Next.js entity-type config (node.page), enable the next_extras experimental revalidate toggle AND set its additional revalidate paths to '/news'. Save both third-party settings to the live site.
evals.expected_output: next_entity_type_config node.page has next_extras.revalidate === TRUE and next_extras.revalidate_paths === '/news' (set both third-party settings and save).
